pill.desc: colorless to brownish-yellow solution in a prefilled syringe

clues.kinetics: Expected to be broken down in lysosomes into small peptides and amino acids, which may be excreted renally, much like endogenous immunoglobulin. Renal impairment does not change its systemic exposure.
clues.substance: Humanized, produced by recombinant DNA in Chinese hamster ovary cells, with a total mass of about 149 kilodaltons. Supplied as a sterile solution in single-dose syringes or vials.
clues.product: Approved under a BLA in single-dose prefilled syringes or vials, given every 4 or 8 weeks.
clues.safety: No boxed warning; contraindicated with ocular or periocular infection, active intraocular inflammation or hypersensitivity. Cataract and conjunctival hemorrhage are common reactions.
clues.indication: Wet age-related macular degeneration, diabetic macular edema, and macular edema after retinal vein occlusion.
clues.mechanism: Inhibits VEGF-A and angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2), suppressing endothelial cell proliferation and vascular permeability. The contribution of Ang-2 inhibition has yet to be established.

tell: A bispecific antibody that blocks both VEGF-A and angiopoietin-2, with a systemic half-life of about 7.5 days.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: Maximum faricimab plasma concentrations (Cmax) are estimated to occur approximately 2 days post-dose
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: The estimated mean apparent systemic half-life of faricimab is approximately 7.5 days
evidence.pk.cmax: Mean (±SD) free faricimab (unbound to VEGF-A and Ang-2) plasma Cmax are estimated to be 0.23 (0.07) mcg/mL
evidence.pill: a clear to opalescent, colorless to brownish-yellow solution
evidence.biologic: has a total molecular weight of approximately 149 kDa
